pages.title: Practice 1: Spot it, fill it in

props.title: Remember first!
props.text: Cover the box. Write down from memory when you use the simple present and when you use the present progressive. Then check.

props.title: Simple present or present progressive?
props.rule:
{{Simple present}}: habits, facts, timetables and states (like, love, want, need, know, believe, think (= opinion), own, have = own).
{{Present progressive}}: actions now or around now, temporary situations, developments.
props.signal: every …, usually, always, never, on Saturdays · now, right now, at the moment, Look!, these days, more and more
props.examples:
Liam play{{s}} hockey every Saturday.
Look! Ava {{is scoring}} a goal.
More and more kids {{are joining}} soccer clubs.
I {{think}} soccer is cheaper. – I{{’m thinking}} about joining a club.
I think … = my opinion (state) · I’m thinking about … = I’m considering it now (action)

props.prompt: Match each sentence with its use.
props.left:
a habit
a fact
an action happening right now
a development / trend
a state (opinion, feeling, owning)
props.right:
Look! The goalie is stopping the puck.
Canada has ten provinces and three territories.
More and more girls are joining soccer clubs.
Liam owns two hockey sticks.
Ava trains three times a week.
props.tip: Look for signal words first: Look!, more and more, three times a week.

props.prompt: Fill in the simple present or the present progressive. The signal words help you.
props.text: Liam is 15 and lives in Winnipeg. He usually [[plays]] (play) hockey on Saturdays. Right now, he [[is cleaning]] (clean) his skates. His sister Ava never [[watches]] (watch) hockey. At the moment, she [[is training]] (train) with her soccer team. Every winter, their dad [[pays]] (pay) a lot for ice time. Look! Ava [[is running]] (run) to the bus.
props.tip: usually, never, every winter → simple present. Right now, at the moment, Look! → present progressive.

props.prompt: Read the news report. Put the verbs in the correct form. Think about the meaning of each sentence.
props.text: Youth sport in Canada is changing. Hockey is still Canada’s game, but these days more and more kids [[are choosing]] (choose) soccer. Many parents [[believe]] (believe) that hockey is too expensive – skates, sticks and ice time [[cost]] (cost) a lot. “We [[don’t have / do not have / don't have]] (not have) the money for hockey,” says Maria from Toronto. “My son [[loves]] (love) soccer, and right now he [[is playing]] (play) in a summer league.” Coach Daniel Lee explains: “Soccer [[is growing]] (grow) fast because it [[doesn’t need / does not need / doesn't need]] (not need) much equipment.”
props.tip: Ask yourself for each verb: Is it a trend, a state or an action right now? Check the box on p. 1.

props.prompt: Each sentence has one mistake. Correct the sentence.
props.items:
She is wanting a new hockey stick. | correct it | She wants a new hockey stick.
Liam play hockey every Saturday. | correct it | Liam plays hockey every Saturday.
Look! They practise on the new soccer field. | correct it | Look! They are practising on the new soccer field. / Look! They’re practising on the new soccer field. / Look! They're practising on the new soccer field. / Look! They are practicing on the new soccer field.
I’m knowing all the rules of soccer. | correct it | I know all the rules of soccer.
Our team is having a new coach. | correct it | Our team has a new coach. / Our team has got a new coach.
props.tip: Check each verb: habit, action now, development or state? Remember: have = own is a state.

props.prompt: Ava says: “I’m thinking about joining a hockey team.” What does she mean?
props.options:
She believes hockey is better than soccer.
*She is considering it at the moment.
She joins a hockey team every year.
props.tip: Look at the last example in the box on p. 1.

props.prompt: If you finish early: The McDonald’s slogan is “I’m lovin’ it.” Explain why this is unusual grammar – and why the company might use it.
props.solution: love is a state verb, so we normally say “I love it”. The progressive makes the feeling sound active, strong and happening right now – that catches people’s attention.
props.tip: Is love an action or a state? What does the progressive add?

props.title: Fact file: youth sport in Canada
props.text:
**Hockey:** “Canada’s game” · expensive (equipment, ice time, registration fees)
**Soccer:** cheap, needs little equipment · popular with families from all over the world · the sport most kids play today
**Trends:** more and more girls and newcomer families are joining soccer clubs · some towns are building new soccer fields

props.prompt: Your school website has a page “Sport around the world”. Write a news update (at least five sentences) about youth sport in Canada. Use the fact file.
props.starters:
In Canada, hockey …
These days, more and more kids …
Many parents think …
At the moment, some towns …
I think … because …
props.checklist:
I have used the simple present for facts, habits and opinions.
I have used the present progressive for at least two trends or actions now.
I have not used state verbs (want, know, love …) in the progressive. I have only used ‘thinking’ for ‘thinking about’ (= considering).
My partner has underlined and checked all my verb forms.
props.tip: Use the signal words from the box on p. 1: these days, at the moment, usually …

props.prompt: If you finish early: Can the sports culture of a country change? Give your opinion with one example from Canada and one from Germany.
props.solution: Yes, I think it can: in Canada more and more kids are choosing soccer instead of hockey. In Germany football is still the most popular sport, but more and more young people are trying new sports (e.g. climbing).
props.tip: Start with “I think …” and give a trend with “more and more … are …”.

props.title: I can …
props.items:
I can choose between the simple present and the present progressive.
I can use state verbs correctly (I think … / I’m thinking about …).
I can write about trends in Canadian youth sport.
